e: ≈ 2/3 of Mendelian disorders are autosomal dominant; AR next, X-linked & Y-linked are fewer
Hereditary spherocytosis: spherocytes c̅ ↑ MCHC, positive family history; confirm c̅ osmotic fragility test (↑ fragility)
Burkitt lymphoma: t(8;14) → c-MYC; 'starry sky' (tingible-body macrophages); endemic form → jaw, EBV
Post-streptococcal GN: subepithelial 'humps' on EM; lumpy-bumpy IF
TACO: transfusion circulatory overload → pulmonary edema (fissural thickening) within hours; treat c̅ diuretics
Membranous nephropathy: 'spike and dome' on silver stain, subepithelial deposits; HBV-associated
Lymphocytic (viral) myocarditis: interstitial lymphocytic infiltrate c̅ myocyte injury (e.g., Coxsackie B)
Squamous cell carcinoma of lung (smokers): PTHrP → hypercalcemia; keratin pearls/intercellular bridges
CLL: small mature lymphocytes c̅ smudge cells → flow cytometry (CD5+, CD19+, CD23+) confirms
APL (AML-M3): t(15;17) PML-RARA; hypergranular promyelocytes c̅ Auer rods, DIC (↑ PT, aPTT)

Hemophilia A/B (factor VIII/IX): hemarthrosis & deep bleeds (retroperitoneal) c̅ no mucosal bleeding.
vWD → mucosal bleeding
Asbestos exposure (asbestos-cement) → mesothelioma; smoking does not ↑ mesothelioma risk
Benzene → marrow suppression, aplastic anemia & leukemia (AML)
Mallory-Denk bodies (alcoholic hepatitis): eosinophilic inclusions of cytokeratin 8/18 = intermediate filaments
IDA: ↓ transferrin saturation, ↓ ferritin; ↑ TIBC, ↑ sTfR, ↑ EPO

Dysplasia: disordered (disorganized) growth c̅ hyperchromatic, pleomorphic nuclei & loss of polarity; no invasion.
Carcinoma needs invasion
↑ β2-microglobulin is a poor prognostic marker in myeloma (ISS staging)
Aschoff body (central fibrinoid necrosis c̅ Anitschkow cells) = rheumatic heart disease
Aplastic anemia: pancytopenia c̅ ↓ reticulocytes, hypocellular marrow (absent megakaryocytes), no blasts
HNPCC (Lynch syndrome) = DNA mismatch repair gene defect (MLH1, MSH2) → microsatellite instability
Follicular lymphoma: t(14;18) → BCL2; CD10+, BCL2+, effaced architecture c̅ cleaved (indented) cells

Caspases drive apoptosis (caspase-3/8/9) and pyroptosis (caspase-1/4/5/11).
Necroptosis is caspase-independent (RIPK3–MLKL)
APL (hypergranular promyelocytes): t(15;17) → PML–RARα
Follicular lymphoma (centrocytes + centroblasts, CD10+, BCL2+): t(14;18) → BCL2 overexpression

Seminoma: uniform cells c̅ clear cytoplasm & lymphocytic infiltrate; homogeneous, non-hemorrhagic mass.
Choriocarcinoma is hemorrhagic
Craniopharyngioma (adamantinomatous): suprasellar mass from Rathke's pouch remnants, wet keratin, calcification; visual defects
Hereditary spherocytosis (AD, spectrin/ankyrin defect): jaundice, splenomegaly, ↑ MCHC, family history
Flow cytometry quantifies CD markers on cells using fluorescent-labelled antibodies
Medullary thyroid carcinoma (parafollicular C cells): calcitonin, chromogranin/synaptophysin +, amyloid stroma; RET/MEN 2
Transitional epithelium (urothelium) c̅ umbrella cells lines the ureter & urinary bladder
Kearns–Sayre = mitochondrial inheritance (maternal): Affected mothers pass the trait to all their offspring, no paternal transmission
Sjögren syndrome: autoimmune lymphocytic infiltration & destruction of lacrimal/salivary glands; anti-Ro/La; ↑ risk of MALT lymphoma

Hepatic adenoma: young woman c̅ OCP use; benign tumour c̅ risk of rupture, so resected.
FNH: central stellate scar, not OCP-related
